seoTitle: AI Language Identifier: 176 Languages with fastText, Offline
metaDescription: Identify the language of text with Facebook fastText lid.176, run by a JavaScript port in your browser. Probabilities, per-line mode, nothing uploaded.
intro: Detect which of 176 languages a text is written in, with probabilities, using the fastText lid.176 model in your browser.
why:
Language identification routes text to the right translator, spell checker, hreflang tag or support queue, and flags pages in the wrong language. fastText lid.176 is a compact, well-known classifier trained on Wikipedia, Tatoeba and SETimes; this page reads its 917 KB file with a hand-written JavaScript reader and predictor and reproduces the reference implementation exactly on our test set.

Short strings, mixed-language text and transliterated text (for example Hindi typed in Latin letters) are the weak spots, and related languages such as Serbian and Croatian blur together; the probability column tells you when to doubt it. The model file is licensed CC BY-SA 3.0 and loads from this site once; your text stays in the tab.
howTo: Paste text; leave "each line separately" ticked to classify every line.
Read the language, its probability and the next two candidates.

faq.q: How is this different from the Language Detector tool?
faq.a: The other tool is rule-based over a few languages. This one runs the trained fastText model and covers 176 languages with probabilities.

faq.q: Why is a short phrase wrong?
faq.a: There is too little evidence in a few words. Lower probabilities flag these cases; add more text.
